Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD), a data-center and PC chip designer, closed at $508.58, up 13.26%. Oppenheimer's upgrade and Google Cloud's chip selection boosted the shares, while investors are watching AI data-center demand and next week's chip-sector earnings. Trading volume reached 50.7M shares, coming in about 123% above its three-month average of 22.8M shares.

How the markets moved today

The S&P 500 closed at 7,556, up 2.43%, while the Nasdaq Composite finished at 25,253, up 2.74%. Among semiconductor rivals, Nvidia closed at $178.67, down 4.27%, and Intel closed at $59.37, up 5.49%, as chipmakers traded unevenly on AI sentiment and leadership scrutiny.

What this means for investors

On Monday, AMD stock continued to benefit from headwinds following the pullback that began soon after it released its third-quarter 2026 earnings report on Nov. 3.

Oppenheimer upgraded AMD stock to an outperform rating, setting a $600 per share price target. If it meets its target, the chip stock would rise by about 18% from current levels.

Additionally, since AMD's data center segment reported a 97% year-over-year revenue increase in the Q3 report, the company's AI outlook has continued to improve, with guidance for 80% revenue growth next year.

Moreover, AMD announced that its fifth-generation AMD EPYC CPUs power Alphabet's Google Cloud's TPU 8tx, establishing hardware-enforced confidential computing for that company's cloud AI systems.

Furthermore, with the notable exception of Nvidia, most chip stocks rose in Monday trading. Nvidia, AMD's strongest competitor in its data center business, faces uncertainty amid an indiscretion involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and an alleged Chinese spy.

The implications of such an act have ripple effects across the industry. Although it remains unclear whether, or to what extent, potential changes at Nvidia would affect AMD stock, AMD seemed to benefit from investors fleeing the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.

title: INTC Stock Down 57% in the Past 6 Months: Should You Exercise Caution?
detail:
INTC Stock Down 57% in the Past 6 Months: Should You Exercise Caution?
Supriyo Bose

INTC
NVDA
AMD
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Intel Corporation INTC has plummeted 56.5% over the past six months compared with the industry's decline of 19.1%, lagging peers like NVIDIA Corporation NVDA and Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD. While NVIDIA stock is down 14.9%, Advanced Micro has lost 2.1% over this period.

Six-Month INTC Stock Price Performance

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Soft Q4 Guidance Triggers Rout

Intel faces near-term challenges as its subdued fourth-quarter 2026 outlook raises concerns about slowing demand and margin pressures. The company expects revenues between $15 billion and $16 billion for the fourth quarter, down from $16.5 billion reported in the third quarter. Management expects Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) segment revenues to decline more than 20% sequentially. Guidance incorporates an estimated $300 million revenue impact from a manufacturing disruption at its Israel facility.

Non-GAAP earnings are projected at 25 cents per share, significantly below the preceding quarter's 52 cents. Non-GAAP gross margin is expected to contract to 38% from 44.1% in the third quarter, indicating mounting profitability pressures. Weakness in the PC market, exacerbated by elevated memory prices and component shortages, is weighing on demand. Management expects the PC slowdown to persist at least through the first half of 2027. Moreover, supply constraints are limiting Intel's ability to capitalize on robust demand for its data center processors.

U.S.-China Trade Spat Hurts Top-Line Growth

China accounted for more than 24% of Intel's total revenues in 2025, making it the company's second-largest market after the United States. However, China's purported move to replace U.S.-made chips with domestic alternatives significantly affected INTC's revenue prospects. The directive to phase out foreign chips from key telecom networks by 2027 underscores Beijing's accelerating efforts to reduce reliance on Western technology amid escalating U.S.-China trade and tariff tensions.

As Washington tightens restrictions on high-tech exports to China, Beijing has intensified its push for self-sufficiency in critical industries. This shift poses a dual challenge for Intel, as it faces potential market restrictions and increased competition from domestic chipmakers. In addition, weaker spending across consumer and enterprise markets, especially in China, resulted in elevated customer inventory levels.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Foundry Business Spurs Revival

Despite the hiccups, Intel is making significant progress in its turnaround efforts, supported by improving execution and growing momentum in its foundry business. In the third quarter of 2026, Intel Foundry revenues surged 58% year over year to $6.7 billion, driven by higher wafer volumes from Intel 18A, Intel 3 and Intel 4 process nodes, along with increased advanced manufacturing activity. The segment's operating loss narrowed to $1.85 billion from $2.32 billion a year earlier, indicating improving cost efficiency. The growing adoption of advanced manufacturing nodes and better utilization of fabrication facilities are expected to strengthen Intel's competitive position and support its efforts to restore sustainable growth.

Intel's aggressive push into next-generation semiconductor manufacturing is another key catalyst for its long-term growth prospects. The company has commenced high-volume production using its Intel 18A technology, while the enhanced Intel 18A-P process entered risk production in June 2026. Intel is also advancing its next-generation 14A technology, releasing the 0.9 process design kit in October to facilitate customer evaluation and chip development. Collaborations with ASML, Applied Materials and Lam Research are strengthening its manufacturing capabilities, while advanced packaging innovations are positioning it to capitalize on rising demand for AI and high-performance computing chips. These initiatives could help Intel attract external foundry customers, diversify its revenue streams and improve economies of scale.

The fallout from a leadership scandal at NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) is hitting one chip stock while its closest rivals hold up. NVIDIA stock is at $176.76 in premarket trading, down 5%. The company's board said it would investigate the relationship between CEO Jensen Huang and a woman the intelligence community believes could be a Chinese spy.

Shutterstock
NVDA Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.

Rival chipmakers are moving the other way. Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) stock is at $464.96, up 4%. Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) stock is at $56.50, up 0.4%, a sign that the selling hasn't spread across the semiconductor group.

Huang's Memo and Board Review Put Key-Person Risk on NVIDIA

In a November 8 memo to employees, Huang admitted to an extramarital affair, apologized to his family and staff, and promised full cooperation with an independent board review. That puts a spotlight on how much of NVIDIA's value rests on one executive. Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives put it simply: "Jensen is the core DNA of Nvidia, and its AI success and ambitions are heavily tied to him staying on as CEO. Jensen is not replaceable."

Beijing pushed back on NVIDIA's story quickly. Bloomberg reported that China's Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun called the spy allegation "unsubstantiated" and "nothing but smears against China." Reuters reported that a planned Korea event involving Madison Huang, a senior director at NVIDIA, was canceled due to "unavoidable internal circumstances at Nvidia," while NVIDIA AI Day Seoul is proceeding.

title: ASML Falls 20% in the Past Month as AI Growth Meets Execution Risk

ASML Falls 20% in the Past Month as AI Growth Meets Execution Risk

ASML
ASML
INTC
TSM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

ASML Holding N.V. ASML shares have fallen 20% in the past month even as the company continues to report rising demand tied to artificial intelligence, advanced Logic and Memory capacity, and greater lithography intensity.

The pullback creates a sharper trade-off for investors. ASML's operating momentum remains favorable, but its valuation, manufacturing expansion, export-control exposure and High-NA adoption timelines leave meaningful execution risk.

Why ASML's Monthly Slide Matters

The recent decline stands against a strong third-quarter backdrop. ASML reported €11.7 billion in total net sales, a 57.5% gross margin and €5.0 billion in net income, while Installed Base Management sales reached €3.3 billion.

The issue is not whether demand is currently weak. Rather, the stock's decline can be weighed against how much future growth was already reflected in the price and how successfully ASML can convert unusually strong customer demand into shipments, margins and cash flow.

AI Demand Still Supports ASML's Growth

Customers expect chip supply to remain below demand through at least 2028, supporting investment in advanced Logic, DRAM and high-bandwidth memory. For 2026, ASML expects EUV revenues to grow more than 45%, non-EUV revenues about 20% and Installed Base Management revenues around 50%.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited TSM plans to introduce High-NA EUV in high-volume manufacturing around 2030 and is working with ASML on larger-format photomasks. Intel Corporation INTC, meanwhile, says High-NA EUV is already being used in high-volume manufacturing on select layers, showing that customer adoption is progressing on different schedules.

ASML Faces Capacity and Policy Risks

ASML expects to ship about 65 low-NA EUV systems in 2026, more than 50% above 2025. Management now believes planned capacity increases of roughly 30% in 2027 and another 30% in 2028 will still be insufficient to meet customer demand, increasing the importance of supplier readiness and manufacturing execution.

China is another variable. ASML expects the country to represent around 20% of 2026 sales, leaving part of its revenue mix exposed to export controls, licensing decisions and shipment restrictions that are outside the company's direct control.

ASML's Valuation Leaves Less Room for Error

ASML trades at 23.6X forward 12-month earnings, above 18.1X for its Zacks industry and 18.2X for the S&P 500 Index. That relative premium means investors are still paying more for ASML's expected growth than for the broader benchmarks.

The multiple is below ASML's five-year median of 31.3X, so the recent pullback has reduced the stock's valuation versus its own history. Even so, continued customer capital spending and disciplined capacity expansion remain important if the company is to sustain the growth implied by its premium.
